html:
The Guna, or Kuna, are an Indigenous people of eastern Panama and north-western Colombia. Guna Yala, "Guna land", is their self-governing province on the Caribbean coast of Panama, including the many small islands once called San Blas. They speak a Chibchan language.

In 1492 the Guna lived mostly in the forests of the Darién and the Gulf of Urabá. Balboa crossed this country in 1513 to reach the Pacific. Over the next centuries, pushed by Spaniards and rival peoples, many Guna moved to the coast and then onto the islands, where they trade coconuts and fish.

In 1925 the Guna rose against Panamanian police who were trying to stamp out their customs. The revolt won them a reserve that became Guna Yala, with its own congress. Guna women are known for the mola, a layered cloth panel sewn into blouses. See also Gunadule.
